chapter: Raymond Scott, Kirby and postwar bands
title: John Kirby as bassist and leader
summary: Leeman describes Kirby as a friend who took Charlie Shavers's advice on his business affairs, and recalls his earlier marriage to Maxine Sullivan and the 'biggest little band' billing.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: You were a premier musician. But I can't think of any better musicians than you were playing with. John Kirby and all these gentlemen that you've named -- these were the epitome. John Kirby had been the greatest bass player.

Oh yeah, and I didn't mention him as a bassist, too. We had a friendship -- it was a friendship organization. Charlie Shavers - whatever Charlie said to Kirby -- was just getting himself straightened out, Kirby would go along with, you know. Charlie, he listened to Charlie, because he did a lot of wrong things business wise.
Is this at a time when he were still married to Maxine Sullivan?
No, he had been divorced. He had been married two or three times by then.
Two or three times by then, yes.
Because he was once married -- John Kirby was once married to --
I know, that's when they first hit. And she made 'Loch Lemond' And the band had white tails, they wore, and ..
Yeah, they had been the biggest little band in the world.
Very close -- the biggest little band in the world, was the way they were billed, the way they were written up, and classed. [PAUSE]
